text:
incident-bot: ALERT — service=redwood-inference-prod route=/v1/generate metric=p99 latency=720ms window=5m SLO_burn=12% — automatic PagerDuty page fired

pagerduty-bot: PagerDuty: INC-2026-8493 generated for redwood-inference-prod (priority: P1). Notifying: @eng-oncall rotation. Link: https://pagerduty.example/incidents/INC-2026-8493

Ava: acked INC-2026-8493. I'm hopping on it. logging into grafana and traces now :eyes:

Devon: I'm seeing a correlated spike in kv-cache misses from the sidecar — eu-west primarily. p95 still ok, tail (p99) up. stack: tokenizer -> model-sidecar -> kv-cache -> model.

Sandeep: @Ava @Devon can someone check the autoscaler logs? If autoscaler suppressed scale due to noisy signals we might be throttling requests.

Luis: quick snapshot from grafana (eu-west):
```
last_5m_p95: 210ms
last_5m_p99: 720ms
kv_cache_miss_rate: 38% (baseline ~6%)
inflight_requests_per_worker: 42 -> spike
```

Ava: confirmed. kv cache eviction rate jumped at 12:07 UTC (TTL churn). looks like a small burst of new keys from a canary rollout. rolling back the canary routing for that model variant now.

Devon: ack, start rollback. I'm also firing a temporary route fallback to model-quantized-v1 in us-east to reduce load on eu-west. Command: `/infra route set-fallback --service redwood-inference-prod --from=canary-variant --to=model-quantized-v1 --duration=30m`

ops-oncall: Noted. I'm increasing the dedicated pool min replicas in eu-west by +3 to buy time — doing a controlled scale up (no autoscale override). Will monitor GPU mem.

Sandeep: Quick mitigation checklist I ran through (from runbook):
- ack + assign owner (done)
- check rollouts (canary rollback) (Ava)
- scale capacity (ops-oncall)
- enable fallback routing (Devon)
- check KV service (Luis)
- customer impact assessment (Ava)

Ava: customer impact — realtime metrics show error rates stable, successful responses still flowing, but latency-sensitive customers (low 99th %) may see degraded responses. Notifying Customer Success for top 10 customers. Drafted note: "We're observing tail latency; mitigation in progress; minimal errors; we'll update in 30m."

Luis: dug into kv-cache logs, looks like a short-lived event where a job warmed up a bunch of new embeddings that invalidated prefixes causing cold lookups. Keys/sec spiked. File attached: `kv-evict-2026-07-12.log` (truncated).

Devon: after rollback + fallback + scale, p99 in eu-west trending down: 720 -> 340 -> 180 over 12 minutes. still watching for recurrences.

incident-bot: UPDATE — INC-2026-8493 status changed to acknowledged by Ava at 12:15 UTC. Pushing to PagerDuty timeline.

pagerduty-bot: PagerDuty: Incident acknowledged by Ava. Next escalation timer paused. If no further ack, will escalate to SRE lead in 20m.

Ava: leaving a short playbook note in the incident ticket: root cause likely bursty key load from canary push; mitigation = rollback canary, increase pool, fallback routing, KV warmers for embeddings. Creating postmortem stub: https://issues.example/RD-12345

Sandeep: can we add a metric alert to detect sudden key churn in KV (threshold based)? current alerting only watches error rate and latency. propose: kv_cache_miss_rate_change > 15% in 2m => trigger low-priority alert.

ops-oncall: added temporary alert to staging now. will push to prod rule after we validate.

Ava: handing off to next on-call @Sandeep in 20 min for monitoring & postmortem follow-up. I've updated the PD incident with notes and temporary mitigation steps.

Sandeep: taking over monitoring. summary for handoff: root cause candidate = canary introduced high cardinality keys -> KV eviction surge -> p99 tail latency spike. mitigations applied: canary rollback, scale +3 eu-west, route fallback to quantized model, warming job queued. timelines are in ticket RD-12345.

Devon: quick log excerpt from rollback command:
```
$ infra rollout rollback --service redwood-inference-prod --variant canary-variant
rollback started: rollout_id=rl-77321
progress: 24% -> 100% (completed 12:11 UTC)
```

Ava: final check 12:47 UTC — p99 eu-west = 160ms, kv_cache_miss_rate back to 7%. closing active mitigation. leaving incident open for postmortem.

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE — INC-2026-8493 marked as resolved by Ava at 12:47 UTC (duration 40m)

pagerduty-bot: PagerDuty: INC-2026-8493 resolved. Timeline: fired -> acknowledged -> mitigated -> resolved.

Ava: created postmortem draft RD-12345 and added action items: 1) add key-churn alert, 2) add kv-warming hooks for canary rollouts, 3) review autoscaler suppression logic to avoid over-suppression during short spikes. Assigning items to Sandeep/Devon/Luis.

Sandeep: will own the alerting and autoscaler item. Devon will own canary rollout changes. Luis will handle KV warmers.

Ava: thanks team. nice quick triage and clean rollback. final note: customers notified, CS confirmed minimal user-visible impact. :white_check_mark:
